title: The deadline moved
setting: Ivan tells his colleague Dana the client meeting is two days earlier.

lines.t: Dana, quick heads up. The client moved the meeting to Wednesday.
Wednesday? That's two days earlier. Where are we with the proposal?
About half done. I'd rather cut the scope than send something weak.
Agreed. Which sections actually matter to them?
That's what I asked them. They said pricing, timeline and the team.
So the market analysis can go. That saves you a day.
Can I run the new structure by you before I write it?
Send it over. I have the bandwidth this afternoon.
Thanks. I'll keep you posted if anything changes.
Do that. And let's not touch it after six, it's already been a long week.

title: Too much on my plate
setting: A manager asks someone to take on another project.

lines.t: Elena, could you take on the onboarding project as well?
I'd like to, but I have too much on my plate this month.
What's taking most of your time?
The two client reports and covering for Stefan while he's away.
Right. When does Stefan get back?
The fifteenth. After that I'd have the bandwidth.
Let's pencil it in for the sixteenth, then.
That works. Can we go over the scope before it starts?
Of course. I'll set up a short call for Friday.
Perfect. Then I can hit the ground running.
